W: Actually, how long will that take? I have to be back at the office in twenty minutes.
M: It usually takes about fifteen minutes to prepare.
W: That's cutting it a bit close. You know what? I'll just have the chicken. It looks fine.
M: Of course. Since it was our mistake, I'll take it off your bill. And would you like a coffee to go, on the house?
W: That's very kind. Thank you.
Question: What do we learn about the woman?

questions.q: What do we learn about the woman?
choices: She will wait for the fish to be cooked.
She ordered the chicken by mistake.
She will not have to pay for her meal.
She will come back to the restaurant later.
questions.why: 店のミスなので代金から外す（take it off your bill）、コーヒーも無料（on the house）。時間が無いので魚は待たない。間違えたのは厨房。

sets.script:
M: So, have you decided which apartment to rent?
W: I'm still torn. The one on Elm Street is close to the station, but it's pretty small, and the rent is higher.
M: And the other one?
W: It's huge, with a balcony, and it's cheaper. But it's a twenty-minute bus ride to the station, and the buses only run every half hour.
M: Well, didn't you say you might start working from home three days a week?
W: That's right. My manager confirmed it yesterday, actually. In that case, the commute wouldn't matter so much, would it?
M: Exactly. And you'd have room for a proper home office.
Question: Which apartment will the woman probably choose?

questions.q: Which apartment will the woman probably choose?
choices: The one on Elm Street near the station.
The larger one that is farther from the station.
The smaller one with a balcony.
Neither, because both are too expensive.
questions.why: 週3日在宅になるので通勤はあまり気にならない＝広くて安い、駅から遠い方。バルコニーがあるのは広い方の部屋。

sets.script:
W: Thanks for coming to the volunteer meeting, Ray. We're looking for someone to organize the charity fun run in May.
M: I'd like to help, but I've never organized an event before.
W: Don't worry. Linda ran it for the last three years, and she's left detailed notes. She's also happy to answer any questions.
M: Then why isn't she doing it this year?
W: She's moving overseas in April. She'll be around until then, though.
M: OK. If she's willing to guide me through the first few weeks, I'll give it a try.
W: Wonderful. I'll introduce you two this afternoon.
Question: What does the man agree to do?

questions.q: What does the man agree to do?
choices: Organize an event with Linda's help at first.
Take part in the fun run in May.
Help Linda move overseas in April.
Write detailed notes for the next organizer.
questions.why: 最初の数週間 Linda が教えてくれるなら、イベントの運営をやってみる（give it a try）と言った。ノートを残したのは Linda。

sets.script:
M: Hello, Valley Auto. This is Greg speaking.
W: Hi. I brought my car in this morning for an oil change. Is it ready yet?
M: Let me check. Ms. Ortiz, right? The oil change is done, but our mechanic noticed your front brakes are badly worn. We'd recommend replacing them soon.
W: Oh, no. How much would that cost?
M: Around three hundred dollars, including labor. We could do it today, but you'd need to leave the car overnight.
W: Hmm. I need the car for work tomorrow. Could I bring it back on Saturday?
M: Sure. Just don't drive any long distances until then.
Question: What will the woman do on Saturday?

questions.q: What will the woman do on Saturday?
choices: Have her car's brakes replaced.
Pick up her car after an oil change.
Drive a long distance for work.
Get a second opinion from another garage.
questions.why: 明日は仕事で車が要るので、土曜に持ってきてブレーキを替えてもらう。オイル交換はもう終わっている。遠出はしないよう言われている。

sets.script:
W: Martin, how did your presentation to the board go?
M: Not great, to be honest. The projector kept shutting down, so I had to restart my slides three times.
W: Oh, no. That room's projector has been acting up for weeks. I reported it to the facilities team last month.
M: Really? Nobody told me. If I'd known, I would've booked the conference room on the fourth floor.
W: Well, at least the board members probably understood it wasn't your fault.
M: I hope so. I'm going to e-mail facilities again myself. Maybe if more people complain, they'll finally do something about it.
Question: What does the man decide to do?

questions.q: What does the man decide to do?
choices: Give his presentation again on the fourth floor.
Apologize to the board members by e-mail.
Book a different room for next week's meeting.
Contact the department responsible for the equipment.
questions.why: 設備担当（facilities）に自分でもメールする、と決めた。4階の部屋は「知っていたら予約した」という過去の仮定。

sets.script:
M: Ms. Kendall, thank you for meeting with me. I'm a little worried about Sophie's math grades.
W: Yes, she's been finding the new unit on fractions difficult. But she's a hard worker, and she always asks good questions in class.
M: Should I hire a tutor for her?
W: That might help eventually, but I'd suggest trying our after-school study club first. It's free, and the older students there are good at explaining things in a way younger kids understand.
M: That sounds great. How often does it meet?
W: Tuesdays and Thursdays until five.
M: I'll talk to Sophie about it tonight.
Question: What does the teacher recommend?

questions.q: What does the teacher recommend?
choices: Hiring a private tutor for Sophie right away.
Moving Sophie to a lower-level math class.
Having Sophie ask more questions in class.
Having Sophie join a free study program at school.
questions.why: 家庭教師はいずれ役立つかもしれないが、まずは無料の放課後の勉強クラブを、と勧めた。質問はもう上手にしている。

sets.script:
W: Did you manage to get tickets for the Northern Lights concert?
M: No. They sold out in about ten minutes. I was refreshing the page the whole time.
W: That's a shame. I saw some on a resale site, but they were four times the original price.
M: Yeah, I saw those, too. There's no way I'm paying that much, even for my favorite band.
W: I heard the band might add a second show because of the demand.
M: Really? Then I'll sign up for their e-mail newsletter. That way, I'll find out as soon as tickets go on sale.
Question: What does the man decide to do?

questions.q: What does the man decide to do?
choices: Buy tickets from a resale website.
Ask the woman to buy tickets for him.
Register to receive updates about the band.
Buy tickets for a different concert.
questions.why: 追加公演の可能性を聞き、メールマガジンに登録して発売をすぐ知る、と決めた。転売サイトは高すぎて払わないと言っている。

sets.script:
M: Hi, I'd like to reserve a group study room for Friday afternoon.
W: I'm sorry, but all the rooms are booked on Fridays this month. Final exams are coming up, so they're very popular.
M: Oh, no. My group really needs somewhere to practice our presentation.
W: Have you thought about the student center? They have meeting rooms, too, and not many people know about them.
M: I didn't know that. Do I need to reserve them in advance?
W: Yes, but you can do it online through the student portal.
M: Great, I'll do that right now. Thanks for the tip.
Question: What will the man probably do next?

questions.q: What will the man probably do next?
choices: Reserve a library room for another day.
Ask his group to meet at the library on Friday.
Visit the student center to ask about its rooms.
Book a room at the student center online.
questions.why: 学生センターの部屋は学生用サイトで予約できると聞き、「今すぐやる」と言った。直接行って聞く必要はない。

sets.script:
W: Your parents are coming for dinner on Saturday, right? What should we cook?
M: How about that spicy curry you made last month? Everyone loved it.
W: I'm not sure that's a good idea. Didn't your father say his doctor told him to avoid spicy food?
M: Oh, that's right. I completely forgot. Well, maybe we could just make it milder.
W: It wouldn't really be the same, though. Why don't I make the roast chicken from my grandmother's recipe instead? It's not spicy at all.
M: Perfect. Dad will love that. And I'll pick up a nice cake from the bakery on Saturday morning.
Question: Why does the woman want to change the menu?

questions.q: Why does the woman want to change the menu?
choices: The man's parents did not enjoy the curry last month.
She does not have enough time to make curry.
The man's father has been told not to eat spicy food.
Her grandmother is coming to dinner as well.
questions.why: 父親は医者に辛い物を避けるよう言われている。カレーはみんなに好評だった。祖母のレシピを使うだけで、祖母が来るわけではない。

sets.script:
M: Ellen, did you get the e-mail from IT about updating our computer software?
W: Yes. They want everyone to install it by Friday. Have you done it yet?
M: I tried this morning, but it said I didn't have enough storage space. My hard drive is almost full.
W: You probably have a lot of old project files on there. Why don't you move them to the shared server? That's what I did.
M: Good idea, but I'm not sure which ones I still need. Some of them are from projects that are still going on.
W: Just move the ones from last year. You can always get them back from the server if you need them.
Question: What does the woman suggest the man do?

questions.q: What does the woman suggest the man do?
choices: Ask IT to install the software for him.
Transfer older files to free up space.
Delete all the files from current projects.
Buy a new computer with more storage.
questions.why: 去年のファイルを共有サーバーに移せば容量が空く、と勧めた。削除ではなく移動なので、後で取り戻せる。

sets.script:
W: Hello, I'm calling about my reservation for the medical conference next month. My name is Ann Patterson.
M: Yes, Ms. Patterson. I see you've booked a single room for three nights.
W: That's right. I'd like to add a night at the beginning. My flight now arrives the evening before.
M: Let me see. I'm afraid we don't have any single rooms that night, but a double room is available. It's thirty dollars more.
W: That's fine, but could I stay in the same room for all four nights? I don't want to move in the middle of the conference.
M: Of course. I'll put you in the double for your whole stay, and you'll pay the single-room rate for the last three nights.
Question: What will the hotel do for the woman?

questions.q: What will the hotel do for the woman?
choices: Let her stay in one room for her entire visit.
Change her flight so she arrives a day earlier.
Give her a single room for four nights.
Charge her the double-room rate for every night.
questions.why: 4泊とも同じダブルの部屋にし、後の3泊はシングルの料金にする。最初の夜はシングルが空いていない。飛行機を変えたのは女性の側の事情。

sets.script:
M: Have you tried the new café that opened across the street?
W: Yes, I went there on Monday. The sandwiches were really good, but I had to wait almost twenty minutes for my order.
M: Twenty minutes? That's half our lunch break.
W: I know. I think they're still getting used to the number of customers. But they have an app now, so you can order ahead and just pick it up.
M: Oh, that's handy. I might try that tomorrow.
W: Just be sure to order before twelve. After that, even the app orders take a while.
Question: What does the woman suggest about the café?

questions.q: What does the woman suggest about the café?
choices: Its sandwiches are not worth the long wait.
Ordering early through its app will save time.
It will stop offering its app service soon.
It is less busy after twelve o'clock.
questions.why: アプリで先に注文すれば受け取るだけ、ただし12時前に。12時を過ぎるとアプリでも時間がかかる＝混むのは12時以降。サンドイッチはおいしかった。

parts.title: リスニング Part 2 説明文の内容一致選択
parts.desc: 約150語のタイトル付きの説明文を聞き、2つの質問の答えを印刷された4つから選ぶ。放送は1回
parts.tip: タイトルで話題をつかみ、選択肢2問分を先に見比べておく。1問目は前半、2問目は However の後（問題点・限界）から出やすい。数字や「〜だけ・すべて」の言い過ぎに注意。
parts.intro: Listen to each passage and the two questions about it. Choose the best answer to each question from the four choices printed.

sets.script:
The Rise of the Paperback

In the early twentieth century, most new books were published as hardcovers, which were expensive and heavy to carry. Many people could only afford to borrow books from libraries. This began to change when some publishers started producing cheap editions with paper covers. These paperbacks were often sold not in bookstores but in places like train stations and general stores, where ordinary people did their everyday shopping. Because they were small and light, travelers could easily carry them in a coat pocket. Critics at first complained that paperbacks would lower the quality of literature, since many of them featured popular adventure and detective stories. However, publishers also released serious novels and history books in paperback form. As a result, millions of people who had never owned books before began building their own personal libraries, and reading became a far more common pastime.
Question 1: What is one reason paperbacks became popular?
Question 2: What did critics say about paperbacks at first?

questions.q: What is one reason paperbacks became popular?
choices: They were sold only in large bookstores.
They were given away free at libraries.
They contained more pages than hardcovers.
They were sold in places where many ordinary people shopped.
questions.why: 本屋ではなく駅や雑貨店など、ふつうの人が買い物をする場所で売られた。小さく軽いことも理由。図書館で無料配布、は本文に無い。

questions.q: What did critics say about paperbacks at first?
choices: They might reduce the quality of literature.
They were too heavy for travelers to carry.
They were too expensive for most people.
They would cause libraries to close.
questions.why: 冒険物や探偵物が多く、文学の質を下げると批判された。重くて高いのはハードカバーの方。

sets.script:
Clever Octopuses

Octopuses are known for being among the most intelligent animals without a backbone. In laboratory studies, they have learned to open jars to reach food inside and to find their way through simple mazes. Interestingly, much of an octopus's intelligence is not located in its head. About two-thirds of its nerve cells are found in its eight arms, which means each arm can sense and respond to its surroundings partly on its own. For example, an arm can continue searching for food in a narrow gap while the octopus pays attention to something else. Scientists are studying this system because it may help engineers design flexible robots that can move through tight spaces. One challenge, however, is that many octopuses live for only one or two years, so researchers have little time to observe how each individual learns.
Question 1: What is one thing we learn about octopuses' arms?
Question 2: What is one difficulty researchers face?

questions.q: What is one thing we learn about octopuses' arms?
choices: They can grow back several times a year.
They contain most of the animal's nerve cells.
They are controlled entirely by the brain.
They are used mainly to escape from mazes.
questions.why: 神経細胞の約3分の2が8本の腕にあり、腕が半ば自分で動く。だから「脳がすべて制御」は逆。

questions.q: What is one difficulty researchers face?
choices: Octopuses refuse to enter laboratory tanks.
Octopuses' brains are too small to study.
Octopuses do not live very long.
Robots cannot copy octopuses' movements.
questions.why: 最後の文：多くのタコは1〜2年しか生きないので、1匹の学び方を観察する時間が少ない。ロボットはむしろ研究の応用先。

sets.script:
The Coffee Shop Effect

Many students and office workers say they concentrate better in a busy café than in a completely silent room. Researchers have found some evidence to support this. In one study, participants performed creative tasks while listening to different levels of background noise. Those exposed to a moderate amount of noise, similar to the sound of conversation in a café, produced more original ideas than those working in quiet conditions. The researchers suggested that a little noise makes the brain work slightly harder, which encourages people to think in broader, more abstract ways. However, the benefits seem to disappear when noise becomes too loud. High levels of noise made it difficult for participants to process information at all. The researchers also pointed out that the effect applied mainly to creative tasks. For work that requires careful attention to detail, such as checking numbers, quiet surroundings are still usually better.
Question 1: What did the study find?
Question 2: According to the researchers, when are quiet surroundings better?

questions.q: What did the study find?
choices: Silence was best for all kinds of tasks.
A moderate level of noise helped people produce creative ideas.
Loud noise helped people think more abstractly.
People preferred working in cafés to working at home.
questions.why: カフェの会話くらいの中程度の雑音で、独創的なアイデアが増えた。大きすぎる音では情報を処理できなくなる。

questions.q: According to the researchers, when are quiet surroundings better?
choices: When people need to focus on details.
When people are thinking of new ideas.
When people are working in groups.
When people feel tired after work.
questions.why: 最後の文：数字の確認など細かい注意が要る仕事は、静かな方が良い。新しいアイデアを考える時は中程度の雑音が良い。

sets.script:
Vertical Farms

In some cities, vegetables are now being grown inside large buildings rather than in fields. In these so-called vertical farms, plants are stacked on shelves several levels high and grown under special lights. Instead of soil, their roots sit in water that contains all the nutrients they need. Because conditions such as temperature and light are carefully controlled, crops can be harvested all year round, regardless of the weather outside. Vertical farms also use far less water than traditional farms, since the water is collected and reused. Furthermore, because they are located in cities, the vegetables can reach stores within hours of being picked. However, the electricity needed to run the lights and air-conditioning systems is very expensive. For this reason, most vertical farms currently grow only crops that sell for high prices, such as herbs and salad greens, rather than basic foods like wheat or rice.
Question 1: What is one advantage of vertical farms?
Question 2: Why do most vertical farms grow herbs and salad greens?

questions.q: What is one advantage of vertical farms?
choices: They do not need any electricity.
They grow plants in high-quality soil.
They are cheaper to run than traditional farms.
They can produce crops throughout the year.
questions.why: 温度や光を管理するので、外の天気に関係なく一年中収穫できる。土は使わず水で育てる。電気代が高いのが欠点。

questions.q: Why do most vertical farms grow herbs and salad greens?
choices: These crops need less light than wheat.
These crops can be sold at high prices.
These crops cannot be grown outdoors.
These crops use the most water.
questions.why: 電気代が高いので、高く売れる作物（ハーブ・サラダ用の葉物）だけを育てている。

sets.script:
Music Lessons and the Brain

For many years, parents have hoped that music lessons would make their children smarter. Recent research suggests the reality is more complicated. In one long-term study, children who took weekly piano lessons for two years were compared with children who took part in other activities, such as sports or art. The music students showed clear improvements in their ability to tell the difference between similar sounds, a skill that may help with learning foreign languages. However, they did not score higher than the other children on general intelligence tests. The researchers concluded that music training improves specific skills connected to listening rather than making children more intelligent overall. They added that this should not discourage parents. Learning an instrument can still build patience and confidence, and children who enjoy music are more likely to continue playing it throughout their lives.
Question 1: What did the study show about the children who took piano lessons?
Question 2: What did the researchers say to parents?

questions.q: What did the study show about the children who took piano lessons?
choices: They scored higher on general intelligence tests.
They became more interested in sports and art.
They learned foreign languages faster than adults.
They became better at distinguishing between similar sounds.
questions.why: 似た音を聞き分ける力が伸びた（tell the difference → distinguish）。知能テストの点は他の子と変わらなかった。

questions.q: What did the researchers say to parents?
choices: Children should stop taking lessons after two years.
Children should study languages instead.
Music lessons still have other benefits for children.
Piano is better than other instruments.
questions.why: がっかりする必要はない、忍耐力や自信がつき、音楽を一生続けやすい、と言った。

sets.script:
Meeting-Free Days

At many companies, employees spend a large part of each day in meetings, leaving little time for work that requires deep concentration. To deal with this problem, some firms have introduced "meeting-free days," usually once or twice a week. At one software company, managers noticed that staff were often finishing important tasks late at night because their days were filled with discussions. After the company banned meetings on Wednesdays, employees reported feeling less stressed, and the number of projects completed on time increased. However, the change was not equally popular with everyone. Some team leaders found that meetings on other days became longer and more crowded, since everything had to be squeezed into fewer days. To solve this, the company began encouraging staff to share updates in writing instead of holding short meetings that were mainly used to report on progress.
Question 1: What happened after the company banned meetings on Wednesdays?
Question 2: How did the company deal with the problem on other days?

questions.q: What happened after the company banned meetings on Wednesdays?
choices: More projects were finished by their deadlines.
Employees began working later at night.
Managers held more meetings on Wednesdays.
Employees asked for more team discussions.
questions.why: 水曜の会議をやめると、ストレスが減り、期限内に終わるプロジェクトが増えた。夜遅くまで働いていたのは導入前。

questions.q: How did the company deal with the problem on other days?
choices: It banned meetings on Fridays as well.
It let team leaders choose their own meeting days.
It asked staff to give some updates in writing.
It moved all meetings to the morning.
questions.why: ほかの曜日の会議が長く混むようになったので、進み具合の報告は文書で共有するよう勧めた。

sets.script:
Thank you for calling Lakeview Sports Center. Here is information about our children's swimming classes for the spring term. Our Beginners class, for children who cannot yet swim, meets on Saturday mornings. Children who can swim at least 25 meters should join the Intermediate class, which is held on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Due to high demand, however, we have just added a weekend section of the Intermediate class on Sunday mornings. questions.q:

Question: Which class should your son join?

The Sunday morning class.
The Tuesday and Thursday class.
The Saturday afternoon class.

sets.script:

If you still have the original packaging, simply bring the item and your receipt to any Homeline store, and our staff will exchange it on the spot. Once we receive your item, a replacement will be sent within five business days. For other questions, please stay on the line.
Question: What should you do?

questions.q:
Situation: You bought a coffee maker online two weeks ago, and it has stopped working. You have the receipt, but you threw away the box. You call customer support.
Question: What should you do?
choices: Complete a form on the company's website.
Take the coffee maker to a Homeline store.
Buy a new box to send the item in.
Wait to speak to an operator.

sets.script:
Good afternoon. This is an announcement from the Main Library. Students can now borrow laptops for academic work. Laptops from the front desk on the first floor can be used only inside the library and must be returned by closing time. If you need a laptop for a longer period, up to seven days, please visit the IT help center on the third floor. You'll need to show your student ID and sign an agreement form there. Please note that long-term loans must be booked at least one day in advance through the library website, so you can't simply walk in and take one.
Question: What should you do first?

questions.q:
Situation: You are a university student. You want to borrow a laptop from the library for one week to write a report. You hear an announcement.
Question: What should you do first?
choices: Go straight to the IT help center.
Borrow a laptop from the front desk.
Sign a form at the first-floor desk.
Make a reservation on the library website.

Welcome to the Harborview Museum of Natural History. Today, we're offering several free guided tours. Our dinosaur tour, which is perfect for families with young children, starts every hour on the hour at the main entrance. The two o'clock dinosaur tour, however, has been moved to the second-floor lobby because of a special event at the entrance. For older students and adults, an in-depth tour of our ocean exhibit begins at 2:15 in the basement. Children can also enjoy our hands-on science corner on the third floor, but please note that it requires a ticket.

sets.script:
Riverside Stadium? Sure. There are a few ways to get there. The fastest is a taxi, which takes about twenty minutes, but it'll probably cost around forty dollars on a game night. The number 15 bus stops right outside the hotel and goes directly to the stadium, but on game days it gets extremely crowded, and the traffic near the stadium is terrible, so it could take over an hour. I'd recommend the subway instead. Walk to Central Station, about ten minutes from here, and take the Green Line three stops to Stadium Station. That should get you there in about thirty-five minutes.
Question: What should you do?
